target: build.js (OWNERSHIP object) + monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md (NEVER_PUSH array) + CLAUDE.md (File Ownership Rules table)
source_evidence: ISS-3011 (poller chg-20260724-0011-004, 2026-07-24): poller's session FUSE mount of monitor/baseline/ showed only 7 of 10 files (08-killshot.txt, 09-audit.txt, 10-review-response.txt absent) and a content-stale 07-ai-context.txt (9,379-byte pre-fix 404-stub vs git HEAD's 32,918 bytes, reseeded by commit b80c1c02 on 2026-07-13). Independently reproduced by tinker-2026-07-25T02-40 on a DIFFERENT session's FUSE mount: identical 7-of-10 listing, identical stale stub, all FUSE copies mtime 2026-05-24. Two sessions, two days apart, same byte-level state = persistent classification gap, NOT the transient mount-view staleness class of DIRECTIVE-20260718-001. Grep evidence: 'baseline' appears ZERO times in build.js OWNERSHIP, zero times in workspace-sync.md smart_copy/NEVER_PUSH surfaces (only discoverability-baseline.json, unrelated), zero times in dome-mirror.md. The git-to-FUSE sync path (build.js sync-workspace, invoked by dome-mirror via monitor/scripts/sync-workspace-step4c.js) iterates OWNERSHIP entries — an unregistered file is structurally invisible to it. The FUSE copies date from a 2026-05-24 manual seed and have never updated since.
problem: monitor/baseline/*.txt (10 dome-page baseline captures, the poller's primary comparison surface) are written exclusively via clone-and-push (poller baseline maintenance, operator reseeds like b80c1c02) but are read by poller from FUSE. Because no baseline file is registered in build.js OWNERSHIP, git-to-FUSE propagation never occurs: FUSE serves a frozen 2026-05-24 snapshot, files added to git after that date never appear on FUSE at all, and content fixes (the 07-ai-context.txt reseed) never land. Poller currently self-rescues by fetching GitHub raw directly, so no analysis has been compromised — but that rescue is a silent workaround, and any future agent reading monitor/baseline/ from FUSE without the raw-fetch fallback inherits 11+-day-stale data. This is the THIRD instance of the OWNERSHIP-registration gap class (ISS-3000 check-wayback.js, ISS-3001 clone-hygiene.sh, now ISS-3011 monitor/baseline/) — the class recurs because nothing lints for git-written-FUSE-read files that lack classification.

options_considered.option: A — per-file OWNERSHIP entries (chosen for Phase 1)
options_considered.detail: Add the 10 monitor/baseline/NN-*.txt files as 'git' entries in build.js OWNERSHIP, add matching entries to workspace-sync.md NEVER_PUSH (a stale FUSE copy must never overwrite fresh git baselines), and add the classification to CLAUDE.md's git-owned list. Matches the exact precedent pattern used for ISS-3000/ISS-3001. Additive, mechanical, zero new code paths.
options_considered.tradeoff: Goes stale if the dome adds an 11th page: the new baseline file would be born unregistered, reproducing this bug. Mitigated by a comment in build.js at the entry block + the Phase 2 lint.

options_considered.option: B — directory-prefix support in OWNERSHIP walker
options_considered.detail: Teach build.js sync-workspace to accept 'monitor/baseline/' as a directory-classified entry (walk *.txt at sync time).
options_considered.tradeoff: New code path in the sync trust surface; walker semantics (deletions? non-txt strays?) need design. Higher risk than the per-file precedent for marginal benefit at n=10 files. Rejected for Phase 1; revisit if per-file lists proliferate.

options_considered.detail: A read-only check that flags files which (a) were modified in git by agent-clone commits in the last N days, (b) exist on FUSE, and (c) appear in neither OWNERSHIP nor NEVER_PUSH nor an append-only walked directory. Three instances of this defect class in one month justifies a canary. Scoped as Phase 2 so Phase 1 (the actual fix) is not blocked on lint design.
options_considered.tradeoff: Some noise risk on deliberately-unclassified files (tracker.json etc.); needs a small allow-list.

proposed_fix: PHASE 1 (mechanical classification, operator-applied or decider self-apply): (1) build.js — add to OWNERSHIP, with a block comment citing ISS-3011 and noting that any NEW dome baseline page file MUST be added here too: 'monitor/baseline/01-home.txt': 'git', 'monitor/baseline/02-wins.txt': 'git', 'monitor/baseline/03-predictions.txt': 'git', 'monitor/baseline/04-coordinates.txt': 'git', 'monitor/baseline/05-model.txt': 'git', 'monitor/baseline/06-evolution.txt': 'git', 'monitor/baseline/07-ai-context.txt': 'git', 'monitor/baseline/08-killshot.txt': 'git', 'monitor/baseline/09-audit.txt': 'git', 'monitor/baseline/10-review-response.txt': 'git'. (2) monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md — add the same 10 paths to the NEVER_PUSH array (comment: git-authoritative poller baselines; a stale FUSE copy pushed back would corrupt the poller's change-detection reference). (3) CLAUDE.md File Ownership Rules — add one git-owned bullet: 'monitor/baseline/*.txt — dome-page baseline captures; written via poller/operator clone-and-push; FUSE is a downstream read replica (ISS-3011/PROP-141)'. (4) After push, run 'node build.js sync-workspace' from the clone (or wait one dome-mirror cycle) and manually cp workspace-sync.md to FUSE per the prompt-sync gotcha. PHASE 2 (recurrence guard, separate implementation gate): add the Option-C registration-gap lint to structure-integrity.md as a read-only daily check emitting a moderate 'ownership-registration-gap' finding; allow-list: monitor/curmudgeon/tracker.json, monitor/analyst/expansion-tracker.json, monitor/analyst/attention-inbox.json (deliberately unclassified multi-writer files per CLAUDE.md).
tradeoffs: Phase 1 enlarges OWNERSHIP by 10 rows (trivial). NEVER_PUSH additions mean a hypothetical future FUSE-side baseline writer would be silently blocked from pushing — acceptable because no such writer exists or is planned (poller is a clone-writer), and the skip would land in workspace-sync-skips.jsonl where integrity 7d sees it. Phase 2 lint carries modest noise risk, bounded by the allow-list.
estimated_impact: Closes ISS-3011's structural cause. Eliminates the silent-stale-baseline hazard for any FUSE-reading consumer. Phase 2 turns a 3-recurrence defect class into an auto-detected one.
verification_pattern: cd $(mktemp -d) && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/funwithscience-org/dome-model-review.git c >/dev/null 2>&1 && cd c && A=$(node -e "const s=require('fs').readFileSync('build.js','utf8');const m=s.match(/monitor\/baseline\/[0-9]{2}-[a-z-]+\.txt/g)||[];console.log(m.length)") && B=$(grep -c 'monitor/baseline/' monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md || true) && if [ "$A" -ge 10 ] && [ "$B" -ge 10 ]; then echo FIXED; else echo STILL_BROKEN A=$A B=$B; fi
notes_for_implementer: Interim remediation already applied by tinker-2026-07-25T02-40: the 4 stale/missing files (07/08/09/10) were copied git-HEAD -> FUSE and all 10 files verified md5-identical to HEAD on the scheduled-session mount (cross-session persistent per DIRECTIVE-20260718-001). That backfill fixes the SYMPTOM on the shared mount only; without Phase 1 the next baseline reseed goes stale again. Do not add monitor/baseline/ to any append_only walker — files are mutable in place (reseeds), append_only semantics would freeze them at first copy (same reasoning as workspace-sync-skips.jsonl's 'git' override). ISS-3011 should be closed when Phase 1 lands; ISS-3012 is a separate assigned-tinker item (priority-queue lint hardening) not covered by this PROP.
